literal: Qin burned and extinguished the Five Canons, destroyed and overthrew the Three Dynasties, changed the former sages, and did not follow the old statutes.
idiomatic: Qin burned the Five Canons, overthrew the Three Dynasties, changed the former sages, and abandoned old statutes.

literal: Therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" of Master Lü shows the meaning of nine chambers; the "Rites" of Dai the Great sets forth the text of twelve halls.
idiomatic: Therefore Master Lü's Monthly Ordinances show nine chambers; Dai the Great's Rites set forth twelve halls.

literal: Han inherited Qin's law and likewise could not change it; the two capitals east and west were both nine chambers.
idiomatic: Han inherited Qin law and could not change; both eastern and western capitals had nine chambers.

literal: Thus the "Yellow Chart," "Comprehensive Meaning," Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others all said nine chambers image the Nine Provinces and twelve halls image the twelve chronograms.
idiomatic: Thus Yellow Chart, Comprehensive Meaning, Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others said nine chambers image the Nine Provinces and twelve halls the twelve chronograms.

literal: Chambers are for sacrificing to Heaven; halls are for spreading government.
idiomatic: Chambers sacrifice to Heaven; halls spread government.

literal: According to conduct one sacrifices; therefore chambers do not exceed five;
idiomatic: Sacrifice follows conduct; chambers do not exceed five;

literal: according to seasons one spreads government; therefore halls do not exceed four.
idiomatic: government follows seasons; halls do not exceed four.

literal: Provinces and chronograms are not what may be taken as models.
idiomatic: Provinces and chronograms are not models to follow.

literal: What use have nine and twelve?
idiomatic: What use are nine and twelve?

literal: Now the sacred court wishes to honor the Way, instruct men, complete rites, and transform by rites—it should take five chambers as the everlasting institution.
idiomatic: Now the sacred court wishes to honor the Way, instruct men, complete rites, and transform—all should take five chambers as everlasting institution.

literal: As for the tangle of temple and school, the miscellany of terrace and pool—Yuan Zhun and others have already argued what is correct.
idiomatic: As for temple-school tangles and terrace-pool miscellany—Yuan Zhun and others have already argued the right.

literal: Later he died as Vice Minister of the Court of Justice.
idiomatic: Later he died Vice Minister of the Court of Justice.

literal: Posthumously he was made Inspector of Jizhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Jizhou.

literal: At first Gui was deeply known by Guo Zuo; Zuo once told his son Jingshang in the hall: "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo—both are talents to steady the state and will surely reach far.
idiomatic: At first Gui was deeply known by Guo Zuo; Zuo told his son Jingshang, "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo are talents to steady the state and will reach far.

literal: All my life I have not advanced men rashly, yet each time I recommend these two—not only to advance worthies for the state but also to make a bridge for you."
idiomatic: All my life I have not advanced men rashly, yet each time I recommend these two—not only for the state but as a bridge for you."

literal: Such was the weight in which he was held.
idiomatic: Such was the weight in which he was held.

literal: Gui because he took squareness and uprightness as his business and Gao Chuo likewise established his name on spirit and bearing.
idiomatic: Gui took square uprightness as his business; Gao Chuo likewise stood on spirit and bearing.

literal: When Gao Zhao was appointed Minister of Works, Chuo went back and forth on calls of courtesy; Gui in the end did not visit.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhao became Minister of Works, Chuo went back and forth on courtesy calls; Gui never visited.

literal: Chuo, not seeing Gui, hurried home and said: "All my life I thought myself without breach of rule—today my conduct falls far short of Lord Feng."
idiomatic: Chuo, not seeing Gui, hurried home and said, "All my life I thought myself without breach—today I fall far short of Lord Feng."

literal: Gui, because cultivating virtue and cautious speech are the root of self-cultivation, while flattery and slander are the great harm of the age,
idiomatic: Gui held that cultivating virtue and cautious speech root self-cultivation, while flattery and slander are the age's great harm,

literal: therefore made the "Four Admonitions": "Cultivate Virtue," "Cautious Speech," "Keep Distance from Flatterers," and "Guard against Villainy."
idiomatic: and made the Four Admonitions: Cultivate Virtue, Cautious Speech, Keep Distance from Flatterers, Guard against Villainy.

literal: The text is mostly not recorded.
idiomatic: The text is mostly not recorded.

literal: His eldest son Weibo, styled Junliang, was broadly learned and had literary talent and thought.
idiomatic: Eldest son Weibo, styled Junliang, was broadly learned with literary talent.

literal: At twenty he was made Erudite of the Grand Academy.
idiomatic: At twenty he was Grand Academy Erudite.

literal: Whenever the court held great deliberation Weibo took part.
idiomatic: Whenever the court held great deliberation Weibo took part.

literal: He was elegantly known to Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Minister You Zhao.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Minister You Zhao knew and prized him.

literal: The Prince of Qinghe, Grand Marshal, Yi, recruited him as staff.
idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe, Grand Marshal, recruited him.

literal: Yi personally made a "Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety" and ordered Weibo nine difficult cases, all raising hidden flaws.
idiomatic: Yi personally made an Exegesis of the Filial Classic and set Weibo nine hard cases, all raising hidden flaws.

literal: Weibo also debated doubtful points in the "Rites," traditions, "Odes," and "Changes" in several tens of items; Confucians all praised him.
idiomatic: Weibo also debated doubtful points in Rites, traditions, Odes, and Changes in dozens of items; Confucians praised him.

literal: At that time the court was about to begin the Bright Hall and broadly gathered Confucian learning to deliberate its institution; debate on the nine-and-five theory long went unsettled.
idiomatic: The court was about to begin the Bright Hall and gathered Confucians; the nine-and-five debate long went unsettled.

literal: Weibo then searched the classics and their weft texts and submitted the "Explanation of the Bright Hall in Diagrams" in six scrolls.
idiomatic: Weibo searched classics and weft texts and submitted Explanation of the Bright Hall in Diagrams in six scrolls.

literal: He also compiled the "Feng Clan Original Record" in six scrolls.
idiomatic: He also compiled the Feng Clan Original Record in six scrolls.

literal: At the end of Zhengguang Vice Minister Xiao Baoyin was Western Expedition Commissioner for the Passes and recruited him as staff gentleman.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang Vice Minister Xiao Baoyin was Western Expedition Commissioner and recruited him.

literal: When Baoyin turned rebel Weibo secretly joined with Prince Nanping Gu and the great men of Guanzhong Wei Zican and others to plot raising righteous troops.
idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled Weibo secretly joined Prince Gu of Nanping and Guanzhong magnates Wei Zican and others to plot righteous troops.

literal: The affair was exposed and he was killed.
idiomatic: The affair was exposed and he was killed.

literal: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou; one son was permitted to enter service—with no son, the grant was transferred to his younger brother Yi.
idiomatic: In Yong'an he was posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou; one son might enter service—with no son, the grant went to younger brother Yi.

literal: Yi's younger brother Shu.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother was Shu.

literal: Shu, styled Junyi, had practical ability.
idiomatic: Shu, styled Junyi, had practical ability.

literal: In the Tianping era he was Director for the Three Offices.
idiomatic: In Tianping he was Director for the Three Offices.

literal: At that time additions and subtractions to old affairs were made in the "New Regulations of the Unicorn Toe"; the titles of laws and articles were all cut and fixed by Shu.
idiomatic: Additions and subtractions to old affairs became the Unicorn Toe New Regulations; law titles and articles were all cut and fixed by Shu.

literal: When Qi received the mandate he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Court of Justice.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he rose to Director of the Court of Justice.

literal: In the third year of Heqing an edict ordered him with Recording Minister Zhao Yanshen, Vice Minister Wei Shou, Minister Yang Xiuzhi, National University Libationer Ma Jingde, and others to deliberate fixing laws and orders.
idiomatic: In Heqing 3 an edict ordered him with Zhao Yanshen, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Ma Jingde, and others to fix laws and orders.

literal: He held the posts of Minister of Revenue, Minister of the Five Armies, and Minister in the Palace.
idiomatic: He was Minister of Revenue, Minister of the Five Armies, and Palace Minister.

literal: Shu long served as a law officer, clearly understood statutes and ordinances, and in deliberation was even and fair; he was deeply praised by men of the time.
idiomatic: Shu long served as law officer, clearly knew statutes, deliberated evenly, and was deeply praised.

literal: Yet he amassed wealth thickly and never gave a portion away.
idiomatic: Yet he amassed wealth thickly and never gave away a portion.

literal: Even to close kin and intimate friends, when poor, ill, and in extremity, he also cut off relief.
idiomatic: Even to close kin and intimate friends poor, ill, and dying he cut off relief.

literal: Public and private opinion of the time greatly despised him.
idiomatic: Public and private opinion greatly despised him.

literal: Outwardly he was square and orderly, yet he could not avoid solicitation; in advancing and retreating to avoid he quite drew sneers.
idiomatic: Outwardly square and orderly, yet he could not avoid solicitation; dodging advance drew sneers.

literal: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei.
idiomatic: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei.

literal: For his son he took in marriage the daughter of Li Shiyuan of Longxi with a great bride-price.
idiomatic: For his son he married Li Shiyuan's daughter of Longxi with a great bride-price.

literal: When the rites were about to be completed they still competed in delay.
idiomatic: When rites were about to be completed they still competed in delay.

literal: Shu suddenly took the image supplied for worship, faced Shiyuan, and struck the image to swear.
idiomatic: Shu suddenly took the worship image, faced Shiyuan, and struck the image to swear.

literal: Shiyuan laughed and said: "Where does Lord Feng always get emergency images that he must swear at once?"
idiomatic: Shiyuan laughed, "Where does Lord Feng always get emergency images to swear at once?"

literal: For his son's marriage he took the daughter of Lu Zhuang of Fanyang; Shu again appealed to the office saying: "The presented horse was faulted as lame in the hoof; the assessed fields were said too thin; bronze vessels were faulted as old and cast off."
idiomatic: For another son he took Lu Zhuang's daughter of Fanyang; Shu appealed, "The presented horse was faulted lame; fields too thin; bronze vessels old and cast off."

literal: All were matters stinginess touched; each time it led to quarrels.
idiomatic: All were touched by stinginess; each led to quarrels.

literal: His son Yuanqian held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.
idiomatic: Son Yuanqian was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.

literal: Shu's younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen, ranged through the classics and histories and held himself by pure plainness.
idiomatic: Younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen, ranged classics and histories and held himself by pure plainness.

literal: He held the posts of Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat and Administrator of Jinan.
idiomatic: He was Left Assistant Minister and Administrator of Jinan.

literal: In every office he had practical capacity and talent; in governing commanderies his reputation for achievement was quite marked.
idiomatic: Every office showed practical talent; governing commanderies his achievement was marked.

literal: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.
idiomatic: He died in Sui's Kaihuang era.

literal: Discussion: Cui Cheng's literary learning and discernment were the excellence of his age; suddenly reduced to insignificance though they thought far ahead—both met calamity.
idiomatic: Commentary: Cui Cheng's learning and discernment crowned his age; suddenly made small, though they looked far ahead—both met calamity.

literal: Xiu in establishing himself had root; in holding office he bore repute.
idiomatic: Xiu rooted himself in principle; in office he won repute.

literal: Changru's beauty of talent and repute—disaster came through arrogant things; though he had the Duke of Zhou's talent, it still became a burden.
idiomatic: Changru's talent and repute invited disaster through pride; though he had the Duke of Zhou's gifts, they still weighed him down.

literal: How much less when one cannot discuss their higher and lower—can one not reach them?
idiomatic: How much less for those who cannot be weighed against such men—who can reach them?

literal: Zhan's phrasing was warm and elegant, his spirit brilliant in emergence—truly men's expectation.
idiomatic: Zhan's diction was warm and elegant, his spirit bright in emergence—he was truly what men hoped for.

literal: Wang Xian, grandson of a famous lord, in old age was seen with exceptional favor.
idiomatic: Wang Xian, grandson of a famous minister, in old age was treated with exceptional favor.

literal: Yuan Jing and his brothers walked the Way and shone in human relations—beautiful!
idiomatic: The Yuan Jing brothers walked the Way and shone among men—beautiful!

literal: Feng Hui could brighten his house's generations; Longzhi toiled in the hegemonic enterprise; Zihui truly raised the hall's timbers—one may call them men who bore virtue.
idiomatic: Feng Hui brightened his clan across generations; Longzhi toiled in the hegemonic work; Zihui truly raised the hall's frame—men who carried virtue.

literal: Junyi amassed and was stingy and mean—perhaps contemptible!
idiomatic: Junyi heaped wealth and clung to it—was that not contemptible?
